question: What happens if a urine sample sits out at room temperature for too long before testing?

options.A: Bacteria can multiply and cause a false-positive result
options.B: All living bacteria inside the container will instantly die
options.C: The specimen label will automatically fall off the bottle
options.D: The urine will turn completely solid within a few hours

explanation: Room temperature is a party for bacteria! They multiply rapidly outside the fridge, which can make a mild sample look like a raging infection.

question: A community health nurse notices a high prevalence of type 2 diabetes in a specific neighborhood. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Close all local clinics since the population is already quite sick
options.B: Establish targeted screening and lifestyle education posts in that neighborhood
options.C: Transfer all affected patients immediately to a tertiary teaching hospital
options.D: Ignore the data because prevalence only matters for infectious outbreaks

explanation: High prevalence guides nurses to focus local resources, screening, and education where the need is greatest. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h6)

question: What important process happens inside the red bone marrow found within cancellous bone?

options.A: Hormone synthesis
options.B: Hematopoiesis
options.C: Filtration of urine
options.D: Digestion of fats

explanation: Don't let the big medical word scare you! 'Hemato-' means blood, and '-poiesis' means making. Hematopoiesis is simply the amazing factory process where red bone marrow creates your blood cells.

question: Which communication approach is best for building personal trust and clearing up doubts?

options.A: Newspaper advertisements
options.B: National television broadcasts
options.C: Billboards along major highways
options.D: Interpersonal communication

explanation: Nothing beats face-to-face talk! It lets you have a two-way chat where patients can ask questions and share their deepest concerns.

question: What must be obtained before starting data collection with human participants in a study?

options.A: A commercial sponsor
options.B: Surgical clearance
options.C: A patent for a new drug
options.D: Ethical approval

explanation: Patient safety and rights always come first. Ethical approval ensures your study is safe and respects human dignity. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h5)

question: When does a pregnancy biologically begin?

options.A: At the first movement felt by the mother
options.B: At the moment of fertilization
options.C: When the mother misses her monthly period
options.D: When the placenta is fully formed

explanation: Pregnancy officially kicks off right when a sperm meets and fertilizes an egg! Everything else follows from that tiny spark.

question: What is the first thing a community health nurse should do when an unusual cluster of sick people appears?

options.A: Wait several months to see if the symptoms disappear on their own
options.B: Organize an international press conference in the capital city
options.C: Verify the diagnosis and confirm that an outbreak is actually occurring
options.D: Close all schools and markets in the entire country permanently

explanation: Before sounding any alarms, always confirm your facts and verify the diagnosis first. Good nursing practice!

question: What is the main public health strategy used worldwide to wipe out onchocerciasis?

options.A: Mass vaccination campaigns with live attenuated virus
options.B: Daily antibiotic prophylaxis for all infants
options.C: Community-directed treatment with ivermectin
options.D: Complete relocation of riverbank settlements

explanation: Giving out ivermectin yearly through community-led programs breaks the transmission cycle and protects village vision.

question: Why must nurses take a proactive approach rather than waiting for problems to fix themselves?

options.A: Doctors rarely check on patients unless a nurse calls first
options.B: Small clinical issues can rapidly turn into major emergencies
options.C: Proactive nurses are excused from doing routine bedside care
options.D: Hospital policies require nurses to document every minor event

explanation: Acting early prevents minor changes in a patient's condition from worsening into critical crises. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h1)

question: What is the correct way to wipe when cleaning a female patient's private parts (perineal care)?

options.A: From the pubic area toward the anus
options.B: From the anus toward the tummy
options.C: Wiping sideways across the area
options.D: In tiny circles all over

explanation: Correct! Always wipe front-to-back. This keeps germs from the back passage away from the urinary opening, stopping nasty infections.

question: What is the main goal of qualitative research in nursing?

options.A: Calculating patient mortality rates
options.B: Understanding human experiences and meanings
options.C: Measuring exact physiological vital signs
options.D: Comparing medication dosages and outcomes

explanation: You've got this! Qualitative research is all about exploring real-life experiences, feelings, and the personal meanings people attach to health events, rather than just crunching numbers.

question: What is the main difference between cleaning and sanitizing?

options.A: Cleaning uses chemicals, while sanitizing uses only plain water
options.B: Cleaning washes away visible dirt, while sanitizing brings germs down to a safe level
options.C: Cleaning kills bacteria, while sanitizing removes grease
options.D: Cleaning is done daily, while sanitizing is done once a year

explanation: Think of cleaning as washing away the physical mess (like grease and crumbs), while sanitizing uses heat or chemicals to knock out invisible germs.

question: Why are malnourished individuals much more vulnerable to severe infections?

options.A: Their immune systems lack the proper nutrients to mount a strong defense
options.B: Pathogens are naturally attracted to low protein levels in the blood
options.C: Stomach acid becomes too weak to kill ingested bacteria
options.D: Malnutrition stops white blood cells from circulating through the veins

explanation: Good nutrition is the fuel for immunity. Without the right nutrients, the body simply doesn't have the building blocks to fight off sickness effectively.

question: Where does the body absorb most of the vitamins and minerals we eat?

options.A: Liver
options.B: Stomach
options.C: Small intestine
options.D: Large intestine

explanation: You got it! The small intestine has a massive surface area designed specifically to soak up nutrients and pass them into your bloodstream.

question: Why are omega-3 fatty acids particularly important in the diet of a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: They support the infant's brain and nervous system development
options.B: They stimulate the immediate release of oxytocin during feeding
options.C: They act as the primary source of daily energy for the mother
options.D: They prevent the mother from gaining too much postpartum weight

explanation: Omega-3 fatty acids, especially DHA passed through breast milk, play a major role in building the baby's brain and eyes. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h3)

question: What is the main job of the urethral sphincter in normal bladder control?

options.A: To sense when the bladder is completely full
options.B: To push urine out of the bladder during voiding
options.C: To stay contracted and maintain a tight seal against urine leakage
options.D: To stretch when the bladder fills with urine

explanation: The urethral sphincter acts like a tight valve, staying closed to keep urine inside until you're ready to use the bathroom.

question: Right after an earthquake hits, emergency food, water, and medical teams are rushed to the scene. What phase of disaster management is this?

options.A: Recovery
options.B: Mitigation
options.C: Response
options.D: Preparedness

explanation: Great thinking! The response phase is all about those fast, life-saving actions taken immediately after disaster strikes.

question: Why does Lassa fever spike during the dry season?

options.A: Farming activities and bush burning drive rats closer to homes
options.B: Cold weather lowers human immune systems significantly
options.C: Increased humidity allows the virus to spread faster in the air
options.D: Heavy rainfall causes stagnant water to breed the virus

explanation: When fields are cleared and burned, the rats lose their natural habitat and move straight into grain stores and residential areas.

question: Why is planning so important on a hospital ward before daily tasks begin?

options.A: It allows nurses to avoid direct patient care responsibilities.
options.B: It prevents chaos and ensures everyone works toward the same goals.
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for emergency staff meetings.
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital will never run out of money.

explanation: A solid plan gives your team a clear roadmap so everyone coordinates their efforts smoothly instead of guessing what to do next!

question: Why does the PMTCT strategy include primary prevention of HIV in women as its first prong?

options.A: Antiretroviral drugs are too expensive to give to pregnant women.
options.B: Men do not play any role in the transmission of the virus.
options.C: Uninfected women of childbearing age cannot transmit a virus they do not have.
options.D: Primary prevention replaces the need for infant diagnostic testing.

explanation: Stopping women from contracting HIV in the first place eliminates the possibility of vertical transmission entirely. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h3)

question: A patient sees a nurse open a pre-used syringe pack but says nothing. What is the main reason for this silence?

options.A: A desire to test the nurse's clinical skills
options.B: Complete understanding of sterilization processes
options.C: A preference for receiving injections over tablets
options.D: Power imbalance and fear of appearing disrespectful

explanation: Spot on! Patients often swallow their worries because they are scared of offending someone they view as superior.

question: How does water move from inside the gut into the bloodstream during oral rehydration?

options.A: It follows sodium and glucose passively via osmosis
options.B: It is pumped across by high-pressure gradients
options.C: It travels through separate channels unaffected by solutes
options.D: It is pushed across by active muscular contractions

explanation: Water loves to follow where solutes go! When sodium and glucose are absorbed into the gut cells, water naturally follows them to keep the balance right.

question: What primary cellular mechanism normally helps move a fertilized egg toward the uterus?

options.A: Chemical signals pulled from the cervix drawing the egg down
options.B: Strong muscular contractions of the outer abdominal wall
options.C: Cilia lining the fallopian tubes that sweep the egg along
options.D: Direct blood flow pumping the egg downward through the tubes

explanation: Tiny hair-like cilia inside the fallopian tubes use wave-like motions to guide the fertilized egg safely down into the uterus. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h2)

question: A nurse uses self-awareness to connect authentically with a frightened patient. Which pattern of knowing is this?

options.A: Personal knowing
options.B: Empirical knowing
options.C: Aesthetic knowing
options.D: Ethical knowing

explanation: Personal knowing is about looking inward and using self-reflection to build a genuine, trusting relationship with your patient.

question: A patient with a history of excess cortisol production is most likely to show which physical sign?

options.A: Permanent darkening of the skin and gums
options.B: Drastic shrinking of hands and feet
options.C: Extreme muscle wasting in the legs only
options.D: Central weight gain and a round face

explanation: High cortisol levels alter fat distribution, causing weight to accumulate around the trunk and the face to become rounded. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why do certain medications need to be taken strictly on an empty stomach?

options.A: To ensure the liver enzymes are completely deactivated during digestion
options.B: To speed up the digestive process in the large intestine
options.C: To increase the overall acidity of the liver portal system
options.D: To prevent food from binding to the drug or delaying its absorption

explanation: Some foods love to mess with medications by chemically binding to them or slowing down how fast the stomach empties, which changes how much medicine actually gets into the blood.

question: Which process completely destroys ALL forms of microbial life, including tough bacterial spores?

options.A: Disinfection
options.B: Cleaning
options.C: Sterilization
options.D: Antisepsis

explanation: You've got this! Sterilization is the ultimate deep clean—it leaves zero living microorganisms or spores behind, unlike basic cleaning or disinfection.

question: Which measure is most effective for controlling vector-borne diseases like malaria in a community?

options.A: Washing hospital floors with scented detergent twice a day
options.B: Eliminating stagnant water breeding sites and using bed nets
options.C: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics to every healthy adult
options.D: Replacing all plastic medical equipment with stainless steel

explanation: Vector control targets the insects that transmit parasites by destroying their breeding grounds and preventing bites. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h7)

question: Why might a mother fail to feed her child recommended healthy foods even after a great health talk?

options.A: She may lack the financial resources to buy the recommended food items
options.B: She forgot that human beings require food to survive daily
options.C: She deliberately wants her children to suffer from malnutrition
options.D: She prefers reading medical textbooks instead of cooking meals

explanation: Correct! Even when mothers want the best for their kids, lack of money can be a major roadblock to acting on healthy advice.

question: What is a primary ethical duty for a Nigerian nurse caring for a patient with abortion complications?

options.A: Refuse treatment immediately if personal beliefs conflict with the procedure
options.B: Delay medical intervention until family members arrive to give consent
options.C: Report the patient to local law enforcement before providing aid
options.D: Provide compassionate, non-judgmental emergency care and stabilization

explanation: As nurses, our first oath is patient safety. We always provide life-saving emergency care with a warm, non-judgmental heart.

question: A 16-year-old first-time pregnant girl comes to her first antenatal visit. How should the nurse behave to make sure she comes back?

options.A: Offering a friendly, confidential environment free from moral judgment
options.B: Requiring an older family member to answer all questions for her
options.C: Limiting her visit duration to avoid overwhelming her with information
options.D: Scolding her gently for becoming pregnant at such a young age

explanation: Teens often avoid clinics because they fear being scolded or judged. A warm, welcoming, and confidential space builds real trust!

question: What does the letter M stand for in the ADME acronym related to drug disposition?

options.A: Monitoring
options.B: Manipulation
options.C: Metabolism
options.D: Mechanism

explanation: Metabolism refers to how the body chemically changes a drug, usually in the liver, which is the M in the ADME process. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h1)

question: A nurse wants to improve sanitation in a rural village. What is the best first step based on community empowerment principles?

options.A: Hold a town hall meeting to listen to community members discuss their main sanitation concerns
options.B: Write an academic paper about rural hygiene without visiting the village
options.C: Order all residents to clean their compounds under police supervision
options.D: Wait for international donors to build modern public toilets

explanation: Starting with dialogue ensures that the community leads the process and addresses problems they actually care about. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is a major focus of nursing research in settings like Nigeria today?

options.A: Designing private space rockets for healthcare workers
options.B: Reducing maternal mortality and improving community health
options.C: Testing luxury spa treatments for hospital patients
options.D: Replacing all clinical nurses with computer robots

explanation: Spot on! Local nursing research here at home focuses on solving pressing local issues, especially keeping mothers and children healthy in our communities.

question: What is the most important assessment to do before giving a patient an anti-spasmodic drug?

options.A: Testing the patient's grip strength in both hands
options.B: Measuring the circumference of the patient's neck
options.C: Checking the patient's visual acuity using a reading chart
options.D: Evaluating bowel sounds and the nature of abdominal pain

explanation: You always want to know what their pain and tummy sounds are like *before* giving the drug so you can tell if it's safe and if it actually helps them.

question: What major staffing headache in Nigerian healthcare do polyvalent nurses help solve?

options.A: A lack of patients seeking medical treatment
options.B: Shortages of specialized nursing personnel in facilities
options.C: An oversupply of doctors in rural health centers
options.D: Excessive funding for primary health care clinics

explanation: You got it! They are a wonderful solution for bridging the gap where specialized nurses are hard to find.

question: What is a transtibial amputation commonly known as?

options.A: Above-knee amputation
options.B: Below-knee amputation
options.C: Partial foot amputation
options.D: Ankle disarticulation

explanation: The tibia is the shin bone, so a transtibial procedure removes the limb below the knee joint. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h2)

question: Which of these is most likely to cause daily, grinding stress that damages family relationships?

options.A: Chronic poverty and financial hardship
options.B: Having too much health education
options.C: Having a strong network of supportive friends
options.D: Practicing good daily habits

explanation: Money struggles put immense pressure on a household. Constantly worrying about basic needs wears people down and sparks friction.

question: Which of these is a common situation that can lead to asphyxia?

options.A: Consuming too much salty food
options.B: Confinement in an airtight space
options.C: Sudden loss of blood from a wound
options.D: A mild viral throat infection

explanation: Being trapped in a tiny, unventilated box or room quickly uses up all the oxygen, leading to suffocation. Always keep safety in mind!

question: What is the main purpose of drug absorption in our bodies?

options.A: Filtering the drug through the kidneys
options.B: Breaking down the drug in the liver
options.C: Sticking the drug to cell receptors
options.D: Moving the drug into the bloodstream

explanation: Absorption is simply how a drug gets from the place you took it (like your mouth or muscle) into your blood so it can go to work.

question: Which drug is a main part of the preferred first-line HIV treatment guidelines in Nigeria?

options.A: Dolutegravir
options.B: Ritonavir
options.C: Zidovudine
options.D: Nevirapine

explanation: Correct! Dolutegravir is a modern, highly effective drug that forms the backbone of standard first-line treatment today.

question: A nurse is getting ready to apply a new fentanyl pain patch to a patient. What important step must be done first?

options.A: Cover the new patch completely with airtight plastic wrap
options.B: Scrub the application site aggressively with surgical soap
options.C: Remove the previous transdermal patch from the patient's skin
options.D: Warm the new patch over a flame to activate the chemicals

explanation: Always take off the old patch before putting on a new one! Leaving the old patch on can cause a dangerous, life-threatening drug overdose.

question: A patient arrives struggling to breathe and has blue lips after inhaling toxic fumes. What is your very first nursing priority?

options.A: Ask family members what chemical was spilled
options.B: Draw blood samples for a complete blood count
options.C: Ensure a patent airway and provide high-flow oxygen
options.D: Document the exact time of the workplace accident

explanation: Always remember ABC! Saving a life by securing the airway and giving oxygen comes way before asking questions or running tests.

question: Which of these is NOT something a community health nurse should do?

options.A: Ignoring community input to enforce rapid medical compliance
options.B: Advocating for fair resource distribution among marginalized groups
options.C: Respecting cultural traditions while promoting health education
options.D: Protecting patient confidentiality during home visits

explanation: Correct! Community nursing is all about teamwork and partnership—we never force things, but rather work together with the people we care for.

question: Which of the following is NOT a normal function or feature of the large intestine?

options.A: Housing beneficial bacteria that synthesize vitamin K
options.B: Secreting primary enzymes to digest complex proteins
options.C: Storing waste material temporarily in the rectum
options.D: Reabsorbing water to form solid feces

explanation: Protein digestion happens in the stomach and small intestine; the large intestine does not secrete digestive enzymes for proteins. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h7)

question: Why does the foramen ovale close immediately after birth?

options.A: The umbilical cord clamp pushes blood into the heart chambers
options.B: Cold air causes the flap tissue to freeze together
options.C: Muscles in the atrial wall contract and seal the hole shut
options.D: Pressure in the left atrium becomes higher than the right atrium

explanation: Blood returning from the newly opened lungs raises left atrial pressure, pushing the flap of the foramen ovale closed. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h5)

question: Why can severe physical stress or a sudden infection cause a high fasting blood sugar reading?

options.A: Infection causes the kidneys to stop filtering sugar out of the blood.
options.B: Dehydration turns blood cells into pure glucose molecules.
options.C: Fever completely destroys insulin molecules stored in the pancreas.
options.D: Stress hormones like cortisol and adrenaline are released, raising blood glucose.

explanation: You've got this! Acute stress triggers your body to release hormones that push stored glucose into the bloodstream to give you energy for a fight-or-flight response.

question: Which type of lubricant can damage and weaken a latex diaphragm?

options.A: Water-soluble jelly
options.B: Natural saliva
options.C: Spermicidal creams
options.D: Oil-based lubricants

explanation: Oils and petroleum jelly break down latex rubber super fast, creating weak spots and tears. Always stick to water-based lubes!

question: How do traffickers sometimes misuse the cultural practice of child fostering?

options.A: It completely stops children from ever attending primary school
options.B: It forces children to migrate permanently to foreign countries
options.C: It forces parents to pay high taxes to the local government
options.D: It is used as a cover to traffic children into domestic servitude

explanation: Traffickers disguise modern-day slavery as traditional family fostering to fool trusting parents and communities.

question: Which sign indicates that fresh fish is safe and good to buy?

options.A: Clear, bulging eyes and red gills
options.B: A strong, unpleasant ammonia smell
options.C: Sunken eyes and grey gills
options.D: A dull, sticky skin surface

explanation: Fresh fish typically has clear eyes, bright red gills, and a clean ocean scent rather than a foul odor. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h3)

question: What are the two major jobs of the human ear?

options.A: Hearing and balance
options.B: Temperature and pain
options.C: Vision and touch
options.D: Taste and smell

explanation: You got this! The ear does more than just let you hear your favorite music; it also contains the balance system that keeps you steady and upright.

question: Why are older adult patients at a higher risk for medication mix-ups during home care?

options.A: Their bodies cannot process basic tap water safely
options.B: They frequently take multiple medications at the same time
options.C: They always refuse to take any form of pill or liquid
options.D: Doctors rarely prescribe standard adult doses to seniors

explanation: Taking many drugs at once (polypharmacy) increases the chance of drug interactions, side effects, and confusion. You'll see this often in community health!

question: A patient takes a daily diuretic medication that causes frequent urination. Why must a nurse note this during a nutrition history?

options.A: Medications have no bearing on nutritional status and can be ignored
options.B: Patients on diuretics are legally prohibited from eating high-protein foods
options.C: Diuretics completely replace the need for dietary fiber in older adults
options.D: Certain medications can affect nutrient levels and fluid balance in the body

explanation: Many drugs interact with nutrients, alter appetite, or cause losses of vitamins and minerals, which a nurse must account for. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h3)

question: Why is it important to have a clear 'case definition' when investigating a disease outbreak?

options.A: It eliminates the need for environmental sanitation and vector control.
options.B: It stops the infectious agent from mutating into a stronger strain.
options.C: It ensures all investigators look for the exact same symptoms when counting cases.
options.D: It automatically cures patients once they meet the official criteria.

explanation: Spot on! A clear case definition means every health worker is using the same checklist, so everyone accurately counts and tracks the right cases.

question: Why do we prefer feeding through a stomach tube rather than an IV drip when the patient's digestive system is working?

options.A: It keeps the gut healthy and stops bad bacteria from moving around
options.B: It is completely painless and requires no monitoring
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of aspiration
options.D: It takes only a few minutes to set up every morning

explanation: Using the normal digestive tract keeps the gut lining strong and stops dangerous bacteria from escaping into the bloodstream. You've got this!

question: What is the main feature that makes a clinical checklist different from a rating scale?

options.A: It provides a sliding scale of quality from poor to excellent.
options.B: It uses a simple 'done' or 'not done' format for specific steps.
options.C: It is used exclusively for grading written term papers.
options.D: It relies entirely on the instructor's memory without written criteria.

explanation: A checklist simply confirms whether specific required actions were completed or missed during a procedure. Nice and straightforward!

question: Where is the main control center or 'thermostat' for human body temperature located?

options.A: The spinal cord
options.B: The medulla oblongata
options.C: The hypothalamus
options.D: The cerebellum

explanation: Well done! The hypothalamus in the brain acts as our internal thermostat, checking our temperature and making adjustments.

question: What is the main job of a flight nurse?

options.A: Repairing aircraft engines and systems
options.B: Piloting emergency medical helicopters
options.C: Managing hospital intensive care units
options.D: Providing medical care during aircraft transport

explanation: You've got this! Flight nurses specialize in looking after patients and giving continuous medical care while flying in an aircraft. Simple and vital!

question: Why is keeping a client's HIV test results completely confidential so crucial?

options.A: It removes the need for follow-up clinical appointments
options.B: It protects clients from social stigma and discrimination
options.C: It stops healthcare workers from keeping medical records
options.D: It ensures the laboratory processes blood samples faster

explanation: You got it! Because HIV still carries heavy social stigma, keeping results private shields patients from unfair treatment by family or community.

question: What is the medical word for not getting enough blood supply to a specific body part?

options.A: Edema
options.B: Hyperemia
options.C: Cyanosis
options.D: Ischemia

explanation: Ischemia is the term we use when a tissue or organ is starved of its normal blood supply and oxygen. Catching it early saves tissue!

question: What is the main job of the Olfactory nerve (Cranial Nerve I)?

options.A: Smell
options.B: Hearing
options.C: Vision
options.D: Taste

explanation: Spot on! Cranial Nerve I is our olfactory nerve, carrying messages about different smells from our nose up to the brain.

question: What does 'expedited partner therapy' mean in plain nursing terms?

options.A: Requiring the partner to undergo major surgery before getting drugs
options.B: Providing medication or prescriptions directly through the patient for her partner
options.C: Admitting the sexual partner into the emergency ward immediately
options.D: Sending a text message alert to all known contacts automatically

explanation: This clever strategy lets you give treatment or prescriptions straight to the patient to take to her partner, especially if he hates visiting clinics.

question: A patient is rushed in with pinpoint pupils, severe sleepiness, and very slow breathing after a drug overdose. Which antidote do you expect the doctor to order?

options.A: Atropine
options.B: Flumazenil
options.C: Naloxone
options.D: Calcium gluconate

explanation: Pinpoint pupils and shallow, slow breathing are classic red flags for an opioid overdose. Naloxone quickly reverses these dangerous effects.

question: What is the primary function of the amygdala within the limbic system?

options.A: Processing emotions and threat detection
options.B: Controlling voluntary skeletal muscle movement
options.C: Regulating basic balance and posture
options.D: Filtering visual images from the eyes

explanation: The almond-shaped amygdala plays a central role in detecting danger in the environment and generating emotional reactions like fear. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h2)

question: Which medication is the go-to first choice for treating absence seizures in children?

options.A: Diazepam
options.B: Phenytoin
options.C: Carbamazepine
options.D: Ethosuximide

explanation: Ethosuximide is the classic drug doctors reach for when treating absence seizures (those brief 'spacing out' moments) in kids. Good to keep in mind for your pediatric placements!

question: What is the main goal of nursing care in a long-term care facility, compared to a busy acute hospital?

options.A: Maintaining quality of life and preserving function
options.B: Performing high-risk surgical procedures daily
options.C: Treating acute infectious disease outbreaks only
options.D: Rapid stabilization and immediate discharge

explanation: Exactly! Unlike emergency wards meant for quick discharges, long-term homes focus on daily comfort, happiness, and keeping residents as independent as possible.

question: A patient is unconscious and unable to swallow safely. What is a main reason to insert an NG tube?

options.A: To permanently cure the underlying brain injury
options.B: To provide safe enteral nutrition and hydration
options.C: To prevent the patient from moving in bed
options.D: To replace the need for routine oral hygiene care

explanation: If a patient can't swallow safely, we still need to feed them! An NG tube lets us deliver food and water straight to the stomach without choking risks.

question: What protective gear is a must when handling strong, concentrated chemical disinfectants?

options.A: Sterile surgical gown and shoe covers
options.B: Heavy-duty utility gloves and eye protection
options.C: Clean non-sterile examination gloves
options.D: A standard paper surgical facemask only

explanation: Concentrated disinfectants can sting your skin and damage your eyes. Always wear heavy utility gloves and eye protection!

question: What happens right in the center of an old TB tubercle as the infection sits there?

options.A: Caseous necrosis or cheese-like tissue death
options.B: Conversion of bacteria into normal flora
options.C: Rapid regeneration of healthy lung tissue
options.D: Calcification into solid bone-like structures

explanation: As the battle inside the tubercle continues, the center part of the tissue dies and turns into a soft, crumbly substance that looks a bit like cheese—hence 'caseous necrosis'.

question: What is the primary advantage of the intravenous route over oral administration?

options.A: Absence of local site pain
options.B: Simpler technique for nurses
options.C: Faster onset of drug action
options.D: Lower risk of fluid overload

explanation: Injecting fluids directly into the bloodstream skips the digestive system, allowing medications to work almost immediately. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina called?

options.A: The cervix
options.B: The fallopian tube
options.C: The endometrium
options.D: The myometrium

explanation: The cervix forms the lower, narrow portion of the uterus connecting the uterine cavity to the vaginal canal, which is the specific site where cervical cancer originates. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h1)

question: If a patient is severely dehydrated, which lab change are you most likely to see?

options.A: Elevated hematocrit due to decreased plasma volume
options.B: Decreased hemoglobin due to rapid red blood cell destruction
options.C: Elevated platelets due to bone marrow overstimulation
options.D: Decreased white blood cells due to immune exhaustion

explanation: When body water drops due to dehydration, the liquid plasma part of the blood shrinks. This makes the red blood cells look falsely concentrated, raising the hematocrit percentage.

question: What do myoepithelial cells do to help with breastfeeding?

options.A: They sense the baby's suckling at the nipple surface
options.B: They build up fat stores inside the lactiferous ducts
options.C: They contract to squeeze milk out of the alveoli
options.D: They produce the prolactin hormone in the pituitary

explanation: Great job! These cells wrap around the alveoli and squeeze like tiny muscles when oxytocin arrives, pushing the milk forward.

question: What happens when you do a task for a patient who can easily do it themselves?

options.A: It steals their dignity and strength
options.B: It prevents accidental falls
options.C: It stops them from getting tired
options.D: It speeds up muscle recovery

explanation: Spot on! Always encourage patients to do what they can. Doing everything for them makes their muscles lazy and chips away at their independence.

question: An NGO wants to help improve child nutrition in a farming village. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Closing down all local markets to force residents to farm
options.B: Conducting nutrition education workshops and supporting local community gardens
options.C: Passing strict tax laws on commercial supermarkets in the capital city
options.D: Constructing a large international airport for importing luxury goods

explanation: Teaching parents about good nutrition and helping them grow their own food empowers the community for the long haul.

question: Why do we generally recommend complex carbohydrates over simple sugars for psychiatric patients?

options.A: They prevent the dramatic energy crashes that can worsen mood swings
options.B: They taste much sweeter and satisfy cravings instantly
options.C: They require no digestion and enter the bloodstream immediately
options.D: They completely cure all forms of clinical depression overnight

explanation: Correct! Complex carbs digest slowly, keeping blood sugar and energy levels stable throughout the day.

question: What happens to vital body proteins if the blood pH moves way outside the normal range?

options.A: They multiply rapidly to restore chemical balance
options.B: They convert directly into usable cellular energy
options.C: They bind permanently to excess sodium molecules
options.D: They denature and lose their functional shape

explanation: Proteins are picky! When blood gets too acidic or too basic, proteins change shape (denature) and stop working properly, which halts important body processes.

question: What do we call using a traditional or home healing practice right alongside standard hospital treatment?

options.A: Alternative medicine
options.B: Biomedical intervention
options.C: Complementary therapy
options.D: Allopathic treatment

explanation: Great job! Complementary therapy means adding practices alongside regular hospital medicine, whereas alternative medicine is used to replace it completely.

question: What does the thermic effect of food (TEF) refer to?

options.A: The heat lost through the skin during a fever
options.B: The calories burned during cardiovascular exercise
options.C: The basal energy used by the liver during sleep
options.D: The energy used to process and digest nutrients

explanation: Your body actually burns calories just chewing, digesting, and processing food. That's what we call TEF!

question: A factory worker in Lagos is injured by a machine. Which Nigerian agency and act handle employee compensation?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Education under the Scholarship Board Act
options.B: Central Bank of Nigeria under the Banking and Financial Services Act
options.C: Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund under the Employees' Compensation Act
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control under the Food Act

explanation: Don't let the long options trick you! The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) runs the Employees' Compensation Act to make sure injured workers get supported.

question: Which drug do we commonly use to boost weak contractions when there is no physical blockage?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Nifedipine
options.D: Dexamethasone

explanation: Brilliant! Oxytocin is our go-to medication because it mimics natural hormones to help the uterus contract more strongly.

question: Which part of the brain stem contains the main centers that control your breathing and heart rate?

options.A: Medulla oblongata
options.B: Cerebral cortex
options.C: Cerebellum
options.D: Optic chiasm

explanation: The medulla oblongata handles the vital, automatic stuff you don't even have to think about—like your heartbeat and breathing rhythm.

question: How does proper health funding positively impact the wider national economy?

options.A: It reduces worker absenteeism and boosts productivity
options.B: It eliminates the need for any private sector businesses
options.C: It forces manufacturing companies to close down
options.D: It increases the amount of money spent on treating epidemics

explanation: Healthy citizens miss fewer days of work or school, leading to higher overall economic productivity for the nation. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is the best and most direct procedure doctors use to check for a duodenal ulcer?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.B: Abdominal ultrasound
options.C: Barium swallow study
options.D: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy

explanation: Well done! An EGD (or scope) lets the doctor look directly at the lining of your food pipe, stomach, and duodenum to see what is going on.

question: Roughly what happens to the size of an infant's brain during their very first year of life?

options.A: It stays the same
options.B: It cuts in half
options.C: It triples
options.D: It doubles

explanation: Amazing! Babies do a lot of growing; their brain volume actually triples in just that first year alone.

question: Why is a skin puncture considered a critical moment for infection control?

options.A: It forces the nurse to use personal protective equipment
options.B: It increases the chemical potency of the vaccine
options.C: It immediately causes allergic reactions in patients
options.D: It breaks the body's natural primary defense barrier

explanation: The skin is our first line of defense against microorganisms; piercing it creates a direct pathway into deep tissues and the bloodstream if germs are present. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h1)

question: A client with severe high blood pressure requests a combined oral contraceptive pill. What is the most appropriate nursing action based on safety guidelines?

options.A: Dispense the pills immediately to respect her personal autonomy and choice
options.B: Double the normal starting dose to make sure the pills work effectively
options.C: Tell her to stop checking her blood pressure while taking the hormonal medication
options.D: Suggest an alternative safe method because combined pills pose high cardiovascular risks here

explanation: Combined oral contraceptives can worsen hypertension and increase stroke risks, making them medically restricted for this client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h5)

question: Why do fallopian tube defects often happen alongside kidney issues in an unborn baby?

options.A: The fallopian tubes secrete fluids that nourish the developing kidneys
options.B: The urinary and reproductive systems develop close together in the embryo
options.C: Both organs share the exact same blood supply during adult life
options.D: The kidneys filter hormones that control the growth of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Makes sense, right? Because kidneys and reproductive organs grow side-by-side in the embryo, a developmental hiccup often affects both.

question: What is the primary purpose of evaluating a community health program?

options.A: To punish staff members who failed to meet performance targets
options.B: To determine if the program met its goals and improved health outcomes
options.C: To increase the cost of healthcare services for local residents
options.D: To make sure no documentation paperwork is ever filed twice

explanation: Evaluation lets nurses see if their efforts actually helped the community or if changes are needed. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h7)

question: A patient with severe cholera is passing profuse watery stool. Which primary supportive nursing intervention takes priority?

options.A: Restricting all oral intake to give the bowel complete rest
options.B: Applying cold ice packs continuously to the lower abdomen
options.C: Immediate administration of heavy intravenous sedatives
options.D: Aggressive fluid and electrolyte replacement therapy

explanation: Cholera causes rapid, life-threatening dehydration from severe fluid loss, making immediate rehydration the top life-saving priority. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h8)

question: Which of the following is a common barrier to effective community health data collection in Nigeria?

options.A: An excess of modern computers in every rural primary health clinic
options.B: Too many trained nurses working in remote village settlements
options.C: Inadequate funding, difficult terrain, and security challenges
options.D: Strict laws that ban community surveys across all local governments

explanation: Logistical hurdles, funding shortages, and security risks often complicate health assessments in the field. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h8)

question: What is a likely result of poor integration between different levels of hospital objectives?

options.A: Increased funding from international health organizations
options.B: Better teamwork between doctors and cleaning staff
options.C: Higher patient satisfaction and faster healing times
options.D: Staff frustration and conflicting daily priorities

explanation: When goals contradict each other across levels, workers do not know what to prioritize, leading to confusion and burnout. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h6)

question: How does a person acquire natural active immunity?

options.A: By receiving protective antibodies through breast milk
options.B: By getting a standard routine vaccine at a clinic
options.C: By recovering from a natural live infection
options.D: By receiving an injection of manufactured antibodies

explanation: Natural active immunity develops when the body fights off a real, live pathogen and builds its own lasting memory cells. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why is it important to test movement and feeling in the fingers or toes below a wound before stitching it?

options.A: To make the skin easier to numb with medication
options.B: To prevent the wound from becoming infected later
options.C: To see if the patient is allergic to local anesthetics
options.D: To check if nerves and blood vessels were damaged by the injury

explanation: Testing distal motor and sensory function helps catch nerve or vessel damage early, before any repair work begins. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h1)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the emergency ABCDE assessment framework?

options.A: Bone stability
options.B: Bleeding
options.C: Blood pressure
options.D: Breathing

explanation: In the standard emergency assessment framework, B stands for breathing, ensuring the patient is exchanging air adequately after the airway is cleared. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h2)

question: A patient with a head injury shows unstable vital signs and irregular breathing. Which part of the brain is most likely affected?

options.A: Brainstem
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Frontal lobe
options.D: Occipital lobe

explanation: The brainstem regulates essential life-sustaining functions including respiration and heart rate. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which stage of dementia usually lasts the longest and is known for noticeable confusion and wandering?

options.A: Pre-clinical stage
options.B: Early stage
options.C: Middle stage
options.D: Late stage

explanation: The middle stage is typically the longest. It brings clear behavioral changes, like wandering and needing help with daily tasks.

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to manage or reduce sampling issues?

options.A: Using a larger sample size to decrease natural random sampling error
options.B: Employing random selection methods to give every patient an equal chance
options.C: Purposely selecting only wealthy patients to make hospital data look prestigious
options.D: Setting strict inclusion and exclusion criteria to keep participant groups clear

explanation: You got it! Hand-picking a specific group to make things look good introduces terrible bias instead of fixing research problems.

question: What is the primary focus of Primary Health Care compared to tertiary hospital care?

options.A: Community-level prevention and basic health promotion
options.B: Providing exclusive care for wealthy urban citizens
options.C: Advanced surgical procedures and organ transplants
options.D: Managing rare and complicated genetic diseases

explanation: Primary Health Care brings essential, everyday health services and disease prevention directly into local communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main goal of antenatal care (ANC) services for a pregnant mother?

options.A: Determine the exact sex of the baby early on
options.B: Eliminate all physical discomforts during gestation
options.C: Monitor normal pregnancy and detect early complications
options.D: Guarantee a completely pain-free labor experience

explanation: Spotting issues early is everything! ANC is all about watching how the pregnancy progresses so you can catch and manage any little problem before it becomes serious.

question: Why do patients with untreated diabetes sometimes experience rapid weight loss?

options.A: Excessive fluid intake flushes away all dietary nutrients
options.B: High blood sugar levels speed up the normal metabolic rate
options.C: Kidneys filter out solid food particles into the urine
options.D: The body breaks down stored fat and muscle for energy

explanation: When glucose can't enter the cells for fuel, the body panics and starts burning its own fat and muscle instead, causing sudden weight loss. Makes total sense when you picture it!

question: Once antibodies are released into the bloodstream, what is their primary mission?

options.A: To lock onto specific antigens and neutralize them
options.B: To break down food molecules in the stomach
options.C: To carry oxygen from the lungs to body tissues
options.D: To form hard physical barriers around open wounds

explanation: Correct! Antibodies act like custom-built locks that attach to matching antigens to neutralize them or mark them for destruction.

question: What is the main job of the thick detrusor muscle in the bladder wall?

options.A: To prevent urine from flowing back into the ureters
options.B: To contract and push urine out during urination
options.C: To filter waste products directly from the bloodstream
options.D: To secrete protective mucus against germs

explanation: Spot on! The detrusor muscle is the hardworking muscular wall that squeezes together to help empty your bladder when you go to the restroom.

question: Why do nurses need to monitor organ function regularly in patients with systemic autoimmune conditions?

options.A: It prevents patients from developing contagious bacterial infections
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future blood tests
options.C: Widespread inflammation can silently damage vital organs like the kidneys and heart
options.D: It proves whether the patient is following their prescribed diet

explanation: Systemic flare-ups don't just hurt joints—they can quietly cause internal damage over time, making routine checkups a lifesaver.

question: A patient with a bleeding duodenal ulcer will likely show which lab result?

options.A: Decreased serum creatinine
options.B: Elevated white blood cell count
options.C: High platelet count
options.D: Low hemoglobin and hematocrit

explanation: You nailed it! Bleeding from an ulcer means losing blood over time, which causes iron-deficiency anemia seen as low hemoglobin and hematocrit on a lab report.

question: External rotation of the baby's head is actually caused by the turning of which body part?

options.A: The shoulders
options.B: The feet
options.C: The hips
options.D: The chest

explanation: Exactly! As the baby's shoulders twist inside to fit the pelvis, that movement travels up the neck and makes the head turn on the outside.

question: How do performance appraisals directly help improve patient care?

options.A: By identifying staff strengths and areas needing improvement
options.B: By removing all clinical errors from the hospital setting
options.C: By increasing the number of patients assigned per nurse
options.D: By forcing nurses to work longer shifts without extra pay

explanation: When appraisals highlight what you do brilliantly and where you might need a little extra training, the whole ward benefits and patients receive safer care!

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing smooth muscles and slowing down digestion in pregnancy?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Spot on! Progesterone is the relaxing hormone that keeps the womb safe, but it also relaxes the bowel muscles, making digestion slower.

question: What makes electrical and chemical burns so tricky compared to normal flame burns?

options.A: They heal completely within twenty-four hours without scarring
options.B: They only affect the outermost layer of the dead skin cells
options.C: They never require immediate medical attention or hospital care
options.D: They frequently cause hidden internal tissue damage beneath the skin

explanation: Spot on! Electricity and chemicals can travel deep inside the body, meaning the damage under the skin is often much worse than what you see on the surface.

question: What is the main difference between focal and generalized seizures?

options.A: Whether they happen during sleep or waking hours
options.B: The type of medication used to stop them
options.C: Whether the patient has a fever
options.D: How much of the brain is involved at the start

explanation: It's all about location! A focal seizure starts in just one spot in the brain, while a generalized seizure involves both sides right from the beginning. Easy peasy!

question: What separates macrominerals from trace minerals?

options.A: The daily amount (in milligrams) the body requires.
options.B: The specific organ in the gastrointestinal tract that absorbs them.
options.C: Their ability to dissolve in water versus dissolving in body fat.
options.D: Whether they are found in plant-based foods or animal-based foods.

explanation: Spot on! It's all about quantity. 'Macro' means you need larger daily doses, while trace minerals are only needed in tiny amounts.

question: A patient on a new BP medication feels dizzy when standing up. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.A: Document the finding as a normal reaction that requires no action
options.B: Encourage the patient to consume high amounts of table salt daily
options.C: Advise the patient to stop taking the medication immediately at home
options.D: Instruct the patient to rise slowly and report symptoms to the provider

explanation: Teach them safety first—standing up slowly prevents falls! Always report new side effects to the prescribing doctor so they can adjust the plan safely.

question: What must a cell do if it makes steroid hormones and suddenly receives a continuous call to release more?

options.A: It must rapidly synthesize new hormone molecules from cholesterol on the spot
options.B: It pumps stored hormones out of the cytoplasm using ATP energy channels
options.C: It opens storage vesicle gates to release a large backup supply of ready hormones
options.D: It stops producing hormones until old supplies are cleared from the blood

explanation: Unlike peptide hormones, steroid hormones aren't stored in large stockpiles. If the body needs more right now, the cell has to manufacture them fresh from cholesterol immediately.

question: An oncology patient on chemotherapy develops a sudden fever of 38.8°C with no cough or sore spots. What should the nurse do right away?

options.A: Apply a warm compress to likely infection sites to check for tenderness
options.B: Encourage oral fluid intake and apply cold sponging to reduce the fever
options.C: Report the fever immediately and prepare for blood cultures and antibiotics
options.D: Recheck the temperature in four hours to see if it drops naturally

explanation: For a neutropenic patient, a fever is an emergency! Because they lack white blood cells to fight back, a small fever can turn into life-threatening sepsis very quickly. Always act fast.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when a patient they are monitoring suddenly becomes unresponsive?

options.A: Check responsiveness and call for emergency help
options.B: Call the attending physician to report lab results
options.C: Administer oral potassium and water
options.D: Document the exact time of the incident in the chart

explanation: In any emergency, always check if the patient responds first and get help on the way before doing anything else!

question: A patient is assessed as a high fall risk. Which nursing action is best to keep them safe?

options.A: Remove all pillows from the bed to reduce soft surface risks
options.B: Ensure the bed is in the lowest position with the call bell close by
options.C: Keep the room lights completely off to encourage deep sleep
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk alone to the bathroom frequently

explanation: Keeping the bed low reduces injury if they fall, and keeping the call bell close means they can easily ask for your help before trying to get up!

question: When you first rush to help a crashing patient, what is your number one priority (the primary survey)?

options.A: Airway, breathing, circulation, and disability
options.B: Past medical history and family financial status
options.C: Detailed psychological coping mechanisms
options.D: Surgical site aesthetics and dressing color

explanation: Always remember ABCDE! Life-threatening issues come first before anything else. If they can't breathe or their heart isn't pumping right, nothing else matters.

question: During which weather condition or season do cerebrospinal meningitis outbreaks typically peak in northern Nigeria?

options.A: Throughout heavy coastal rainfall
options.B: During the dry harmattan season
options.C: During periods of extreme flooding
options.D: In the middle of the humid summer

explanation: Dry, dusty harmattan winds irritate the upper respiratory lining, making it easier for bacteria to invade and cause meningitis. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h3)

question: How does hospital underfunding directly affect patient recovery outcomes?

options.A: It lowers the cost of prescription medications
options.B: It guarantees faster healing through natural immunity
options.C: It increases mortality rates and prolongs hospital stays
options.D: It prevents patients from contracting hospital infections

explanation: Lack of supplies, broken equipment, and overworked staff lead to delayed care and worse health outcomes for patients. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h5)

question: What nursing action should be completed just before the procedure starts?

options.A: Place the patient flat on their back with pillows
options.B: Shave the entire back from shoulders to hips
options.C: Administer a strong sleeping pill by mouth
options.D: Ask the patient to empty their urinary bladder

explanation: Correct! An empty bladder keeps the patient comfortable while they stay curled up in a tight position during the test.

question: Which type of early pregnancy loss features vaginal bleeding while the cervix remains firmly closed?

options.A: Threatened abortion
options.B: Inevitable abortion
options.C: Complete abortion
options.D: Incomplete abortion

explanation: In a threatened abortion, there's some bleeding, but because the cervix is still closed, there's still a strong chance the pregnancy can continue safely.

question: What is the main goal of using an open-ended question when talking to a patient?

options.A: To let patients tell their story in their own words
options.B: To test the patient's memory on past surgeries
options.C: To get a quick yes or no answer about a symptom
options.D: To confirm the exact date a medication was started

explanation: You got it! Open-ended questions give patients the freedom to express their concerns naturally without feeling rushed or boxed in.

question: A patient gets schistosomiasis after wading in a slow-moving stream. How did they catch it?

options.A: A bite from an aquatic insect vector
options.B: Water-contact with free-swimming larvae
options.C: Inhalation of steam near the water
options.D: Ingestion of undercooked river fish

explanation: Schistosoma parasites release tiny larvae into freshwater. If someone wades or bathes in that water, the larvae swim right up and penetrate their skin. Nature can be tricky!

question: What is the main goal of giving 'phosphate binders' to a patient with kidney failure?

options.A: To lower systemic blood pressure by relaxing blood vessel walls
options.B: To prevent dietary phosphorus from being absorbed in the gut
options.C: To increase daily urine output and reduce swelling in the legs
options.D: To stimulate red blood cell production in the bone marrow

explanation: Patients take these binders right with their meals. The medicine grabs onto phosphorus in the food and carries it out safely through the stool so it doesn't flood the blood.

question: What is the main danger associated with postpartum hemorrhage in new mothers?

options.A: Permanent loss of the ability to walk
options.B: Severe allergic reactions to routine food
options.C: Chronic high blood pressure lasting years
options.D: Sudden and severe blood loss leading to shock

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage involves heavy bleeding after birth, which can quickly drop blood pressure and cause life-threatening shock if untreated. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h2)

question: What special feature in modern surgical swabs helps find them easily on an X-ray?

options.A: A built-in electronic tracking chip
options.B: A bright fluorescent dye coating
options.C: A radiopaque marker strip
options.D: A magnetic metallic button

explanation: Radiopaque strips show up brightly on X-ray machines, acting like a safety net if a swab ever goes missing.

question: What is a community health nurse's main job during early disease surveillance?

options.A: Detecting and reporting unusual symptom clusters
options.B: Declaring a national state of emergency
options.C: Manufacturing vaccines for the community
options.D: Treating severe cases in intensive care units

explanation: You're doing great! Nurses act as our frontline watchdogs by spotting unusual health patterns early and reporting them.

question: Where in the female reproductive tract does fertilization most commonly take place?

options.A: Vaginal canal
options.B: Fallopian tube
options.C: Ovarian surface
options.D: Uterine cavity

explanation: The ampulla of the fallopian tube is the usual meeting place for the sperm and the egg. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h3)

question: In pathology, what exactly is a granuloma?

options.A: A rapid swelling of blood vessels caused by an acute bacterial toxin
options.B: An open sore on the mucous membrane caused by digestive acid
options.C: A sudden, fluid-filled blister caused by a viral skin infection
options.D: A walled-off collection of modified macrophages and immune cells fighting a persistent germ

explanation: When the body can't easily destroy a stubborn germ (like TB), immune cells group together to wall it off in a little fort called a granuloma.

question: Which type of financial control happens BEFORE an expense actually occurs?

options.A: Punitive control
options.B: Detective control
options.C: Corrective control
options.D: Preventive control

explanation: Just like prevention in nursing care, preventive controls are set up beforehand to stop mistakes or bad spending before they happen.

question: A hospital ward has a broken fan, uncomfortable chairs, and delayed salaries, making the nurses very upset. What do these represent in Herzberg's theory?

options.A: Hygiene factors causing job dissatisfaction
options.B: Self-actualization blocks in Maslow's pyramid
options.C: Motivators driving professional growth
options.D: Intrinsic rewards missing from daily tasks

explanation: When basic things like pay and a comfortable environment are messed up, workers get frustrated right away—no matter how much they love nursing!

question: How might personal or religious stigma poorly show up in a nurse during PAC care?

options.A: Prescribing higher doses of antibiotics to punish the patient
options.B: Mandating public community service for every PAC client
options.C: Displaying coldness, disapproval, or open hostility toward the client
options.D: Refusing to document the patient's vital signs on the chart

explanation: Sometimes nurses let personal beliefs slip out through cold sighs, dirty looks, or harsh remarks, which really hurts a vulnerable patient.

question: Which electrical shift makes the heart muscle cells contract?

options.A: Hyperpolarization
options.B: Repolarization
options.C: Depolarization
options.D: Polarization

explanation: Depolarization is just the electrical spark where positive ions rush in, making the heart muscle squeeze!

question: Why is tracking a child's growth over several visits better than just taking one weight measurement?

options.A: Children never change their weight during growth spurts
options.B: Growth charts are completely inaccurate for children under five years old
options.C: A steady pattern shows normal development better than one isolated number
options.D: A single measurement only shows fluid balance, not true growth

explanation: Great thinking! Checking growth over time gives you the real trend rather than stressing over a single random number. Nursing is all about the big picture!

question: Why do nurses and dietitians use activity multipliers along with a patient's BMR?

options.A: To correct for errors in food label calorie counts
options.B: To determine the patient's exact vitamin requirements
options.C: To account for daily movement and exercise energy costs
options.D: To calculate the exact amount of daily water loss

explanation: BMR only covers resting in bed. Activity multipliers help us estimate the extra calories burned walking around or doing physical therapy.

question: What does a serum ferritin blood test tell the healthcare team?

options.A: Circulating blood sugar
options.B: Active vitamin B12 levels
options.C: Red blood cell lifespan
options.D: Stored iron reserves

explanation: Think of ferritin as the body's iron savings account. A serum ferritin test lets you see how much iron is safely tucked away in storage.

question: How does adrenaline directly affect blood flow to the uterus when a mum is stressed?

options.A: It stops all electrical activity in the myometrium instantly
options.B: It dilates blood vessels to increase oxygen delivery to the fetus
options.C: It converts glucose into amniotic fluid rapidly
options.D: It constricts blood vessels and reduces blood flow to the uterus

explanation: Stress hormones cause blood vessels to tighten up (vasoconstriction), drawing blood away from the womb and sending it to the big muscles instead.

question: Why is a lack of fair disciplinary structures dangerous in a hospital ward?

options.A: It forces nurses to work longer shifts
options.B: it causes immediate resignation of all doctors
options.C: It leads to clinical chaos and poor patient safety
options.D: It automatically increases the hospital budget

explanation: Without rules and corrective action, standards drop, putting patient lives at direct risk. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h1)

question: What is a major structural difference between sympathetic and parasympathetic pathways?

options.A: Sympathetic fibers never use ganglia to pass signals along.
options.B: Sympathetic preganglionic fibers are always much longer than postganglionic fibers.
options.C: Parasympathetic nerves only exit through the lumbar spinal cord.
options.D: Parasympathetic ganglia are usually located close to or inside the target organs.

explanation: Because parasympathetic fibers travel a long way from the brain or lower spine before reaching their destination, their relay stations (ganglia) sit right near or inside the target organ walls.

question: A woman in labor is having strong contractions. Which part of her uterine wall is doing all that hard work?

options.A: Perimetrium
options.B: Endometrium
options.C: Myometrium
options.D: Cervical os

explanation: Spot on! The myometrium is made of tough, powerful smooth muscle designed to push the baby safely into the world.

question: What does direct calorimetry measure to determine energy expenditure?

options.A: Heat produced by the body
options.B: Carbon dioxide exhaled in breath
options.C: Oxygen inhaled through a mask
options.D: Nitrogen lost in urine samples

explanation: Direct calorimetry calculates energy use by measuring the actual heat given off by a person inside a special chamber. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h6)

question: Why must you watch the baby closely with a CTG machine when giving an oxytocin drip?

options.A: Oxytocin makes the baby sleep deeply throughout the entire procedure.
options.B: Oxytocin causes the cervix to close up instead of opening further.
options.C: Oxytocin permanently lowers the mother's blood pressure to dangerous levels.
options.D: Oxytocin can cause uterine hyperstimulation, leading to reduced blood flow and fetal distress.

explanation: Spot on! Too much oxytocin can make contractions come too fast without resting breaks, cutting off oxygen to the baby. Safety first!

question: Why can taking a health history for hormone problems be tricky for a nurse?

options.A: Symptoms are usually vague and overlap across different disorders
options.B: Patients almost never remember when their symptoms started
options.C: Endocrine problems only affect one specific body system at a time
options.D: Laboratory tests are completely useless without a physical exam

explanation: You got it! Hormonal issues often start with everyday complaints like constant tiredness, making it hard to pin down the exact cause without patient probing.

question: Why must nurses rely on evidence-based practice when discussing complementary therapies with patients?

options.A: To ensure the chosen therapies are genuinely safe and effective
options.B: To force patients to stop using all traditional cultural customs
options.C: Because hospital management fines nurses who mention herbs
options.D: Because scientific journals require annual subscriptions

explanation: Brilliant! Evidence-based practice helps protect our patients from harmful trends and guides them toward truly helpful supportive care.

question: Why is regular walking encouraged for patients with stable peripheral artery disease?

options.A: It forces venous blood upward by squeezing calf muscles
options.B: It helps tiny new blood vessels (collateral vessels) grow around blockages
options.C: It melts away calcified plaque in the leg arteries
options.D: It lowers heart rate and stops vasospasms

explanation: Exercise stimulates the body to build little detour pathways around blocked arteries! These collateral vessels bring fresh oxygen to leg muscles over time.

question: Which life stage has the fastest human growth rate, coming in second right after infancy?

options.A: Adolescence
options.B: Toddlerhood
options.C: Young adulthood
options.D: Middle childhood

explanation: You've got this! Adolescence is well known as the second fastest period of human growth, right behind infancy. Your body is doing amazing things during these teenage years!

question: How do infections inside the uterus trigger early labour?

options.A: By causing a sudden drop in circulating maternal red blood cells
options.B: By blocking the normal production of maternal thyroid hormones
options.C: By increasing the thickness of the amniotic fluid membranes
options.D: By releasing pro-inflammatory cytokines that stimulate prostaglandins

explanation: When an infection stirs up the immune system, it releases inflammatory chemicals that act like a wake-up call for prostaglandins, triggering contractions. You're mastering the patho!

question: What simple tool do nurses use to quickly spot acute malnutrition in toddlers?

options.A: Stethoscope and blood pressure cuff
options.B: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference tape
options.C: Neurological reflex hammer
options.D: Electrocardiogram leads

explanation: MUAC is a fast, reliable, and portable way to screen young children for malnutrition in community settings. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h3)

question: Why do nurses always warm up peritoneal dialysis fluids before infusing them?

options.A: To kill any bacteria present in the plastic tubing
options.B: To prevent abdominal cramping and patient hypothermia
options.C: To prevent the fluid from turning into a solid gel
options.D: To make the drug dissolve faster inside the IV bag

explanation: Exactly! Putting cold fluid straight into the belly causes painful cramps and can drop the patient's body temperature. Always warm it to body temperature first! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h5)

question: What is an important nursing task to do right after a patient finishes eating to lower their risk of pneumonia?

options.A: Encouraging immediate strenuous walking
options.B: Lowering the head of the bed completely
options.C: Offering a large glass of thin water
options.D: Providing thorough oral hygiene

explanation: Brushing the teeth and cleaning the mouth clears away leftover food bits and bacteria that could otherwise slip into the lungs later.

question: What do deep, wide Q waves usually point to on an ECG?

options.A: Myocardial infarction and tissue necrosis
options.B: Temporary lack of oxygen called ischemia
options.C: Atrial enlargement from high blood pressure
options.D: Normal athletic heart enlargement

explanation: Those deep Q waves are like footprints left behind when a part of the heart muscle has unfortunately died off.

question: What is the primary role of traditional and religious leaders in policy implementation?

options.A: Aiding social mobilization and gaining community acceptance
options.B: Drafting legal amendments for the national parliament
options.C: Conducting surgical family planning procedures in clinics
options.D: Auditing government budgets for health infrastructure

explanation: People trust their local and religious leaders. When these leaders support health initiatives, community members are much more open to listening and participating.

question: What is the most crucial lifestyle habit a nurse must teach a patient taking a cystine-binding drug?

options.A: Restricting all protein intake completely from the diet
options.B: Avoiding exposure to direct sunlight during daytime hours
options.C: Engaging in high-intensity aerobic exercise to sweat out toxins
options.D: Maintaining a very high daily fluid intake to dilute the urine

explanation: Water is the best medicine here! Pills alone can't stop stones if the urine is super concentrated. Pushing fluids dilutes the urine so crystals can't form.

question: Which record book requires the strictest tracking for strong medications like morphine?

options.A: Visitor arrival sheet
options.B: Narcotic logbook
options.C: Patient dietary ledger
options.D: General laundry register

explanation: Controlled drugs like narcotics are strictly monitored using a dedicated logbook with continuous counts to prevent any loss or misuse.

question: You feel an organ extending past the left rib margin during a deep abdominal exam. What organ are you most likely feeling?

options.A: Kidney
options.B: Liver
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Spleen

explanation: The spleen hangs out in the upper left side of the abdomen. If it's enlarged, it extends downward from beneath the left ribs where you can feel it.

question: Why would a surgeon leave an amputation wound open instead of stitching the skin right away?

options.A: To allow drainage and prevent trapping severe infection inside the wound
options.B: To stretch the skin flaps so they cover a larger area of bone
options.C: To give the patient time to practice moving the joint before closure
options.D: To make it easier to fit a temporary plastic cast on the bone

explanation: If there's an infection present, closing the skin immediately would trap bacteria inside and cause abscesses. Leaving it open temporarily keeps things safe!

question: What is considered a nurse's best legal defense in a malpractice lawsuit?

options.A: Claiming that the hospital was too busy to provide safe care
options.B: Destroying the hospital incident report before lawyers arrive
options.C: Clear, accurate, and objective documentation in the client's medical record
options.D: Blaming the junior nursing students for routine ward errors

explanation: Contemporaneous and factual nursing notes provide clear proof of the care delivered when legal disputes arise. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h8)

question: What is the name of the hollow ball of cells that gets ready to implant in the uterus?

options.A: Secondary oocyte
options.B: Corpus luteum
options.C: Zygote
options.D: Blastocyst

explanation: The blastocyst is the stage of early development that hatches from its outer shell and successfully nests into the lining of the womb.

question: What is the primary purpose of a stock card in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To record the daily vital signs and health status of admitted patients
options.B: To document the financial salaries and allowances of hospital workers
options.C: To schedule the duty shifts and off-days of the ward nursing staff
options.D: To track the exact quantity and movement of a specific supply item

explanation: A stock card functions as a ledger specifically designed to monitor inventory levels, showing when items enter and leave the ward. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)

question: Why is drug synergism especially helpful when fighting bacterial infections?

options.A: It helps prevent or delay the development of drug resistance
options.B: It guarantees that side effects will never occur
options.C: It eliminates the need for any patient fluid intake
options.D: It turns antibiotics into vitamins that nourish body tissues

explanation: When we attack germs on multiple fronts at once, it makes it super difficult for them to mutate and build resistance to our drugs.

question: A community health nurse is teaching villagers how Ebola spreads. Which practice should she warn against the most?

options.A: Drinking boiled water from a community well during dry seasons
options.B: Eating well-cooked pork from certified local livestock farms
options.C: Washing the body of a relative who died from suspected Ebola
options.D: Sharing eating utensils with a family member who has malaria

explanation: Well done! The viral load is super high in someone who just passed away, making traditional burial touching very risky.

question: How do non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) help relieve pain?

options.A: Blocking prostaglandins to reduce pain and swelling
options.B: Destroying bacteria directly in the bloodstream
options.C: Permanently stopping all white blood cell production
options.D: Freezing the skin to numb local nerve endings

explanation: You nailed it! NSAIDs stop the body from making prostaglandins, which are the chemical messengers of pain and swelling.

question: Which of the following is a well-known harmful traditional practice that involves the partial or total removal of external female genitalia?

options.A: Obstetric fistula repair
options.B: Female genital mutilation
options.C: Prenatal vitamin supplementation
options.D: Traditional scarification therapy

explanation: Female genital mutilation is a recognized harmful traditional practice causing severe long-term health complications for women and girls. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h6)

question: What happens when stock levels drop below a safe minimum in an electronic inventory system?

options.A: An automatic reorder alert is generated
options.B: The hospital power generator shuts down automatically
options.C: All patient charts are locked until new stock arrives
options.D: The nursing supervisor's license is suspended
