explanation: Electronic systems track thresholds and notify purchasing staff to reorder items before they run out completely. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h3)

question: A patient suddenly starts wheezing, develops hives, and has facial swelling ten minutes after an injection. What should you do right away?

options.A: Tell the client to walk home quickly and rest in bed
options.B: Wait another hour to see if the symptoms disappear on their own
options.C: Administer intramuscular epinephrine and monitor vital signs
options.D: Document the mild local reaction and send the client away

explanation: These are classic signs of anaphylaxis. Quick action with intramuscular epinephrine can prevent the airway from closing up.

question: What is the literal meaning of the word 'pons'?

options.A: Bridge
options.B: Tunnel
options.C: Pillar
options.D: Gateway

explanation: The term pons translates to bridge, reflecting its anatomical job of connecting different regions of the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T20#GNS211_U3_T20_h1)

question: A patient insists on receiving an injection for a mild headache instead of taking paracetamol tablets. What drives this demand?

options.A: A diagnosed severe allergy to all oral analgesic medications
options.B: Cultural perception that needles equal superior medical treatment
options.C: Hospital protocol requiring injections for all reported pain
options.D: Immediate renal failure requiring rapid parenteral hydration

explanation: Patients often associate the physical action of an injection with high-value care, leading to unnecessary demands. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h2)

question: For a rural farming community starting a health fund, when is the best time to collect annual insurance dues?

options.A: Only when a member falls seriously ill
options.B: During harvest seasons when cash flow is highest
options.C: During the dry season when crop failure occurs
options.D: Every single week without exception

explanation: Smart planning! Timing contributions with income cycles makes sure members actually have the cash on hand to pay their dues.

question: Why do viral infections usually NOT produce thick pus the way bacterial infections do?

options.A: Viruses live strictly on the outer surface of the skin where pus cannot form.
options.B: Viruses only infect red blood cells, which lack the ability to cause inflammation.
options.C: Viruses instantly destroy all white blood cells in the human body on contact.
options.D: Viruses do not recruit large numbers of pus-forming neutrophils in the same way pyogenic bacteria do.

explanation: Pus is mostly packed with neutrophils responding to bacteria. Viruses trigger a different immune response, so you don't get that classic thick pus.

question: What is often one of the very first warning signs of dehydration in an elderly patient?

options.A: Sudden confusion or altered mental status
options.B: Swelling in the feet and lower ankles
options.C: Severe itching all over the skin surface
options.D: A sudden increase in appetite and weight

explanation: It's easy to miss, but sudden confusion is a classic red flag for dehydration in older adults! Always check hydration status when an elderly patient's mood or alertness changes.

question: What is the main purpose of a team charter in a quality improvement project?

options.A: Recording daily nursing shift handover notes and updates
options.B: Acting as a roadmap that defines project scope and goals
options.C: Listing disciplinary actions for missed project deadlines
options.D: Determining annual salary increases for clinical staff

explanation: Correct! A team charter sets clear goals and boundaries so everyone stays focused on the same target from day one.

question: An elderly male patient after surgery is restless and feels a strong urge to pee, but nothing comes out. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Stress incontinence
options.B: Renal tubular acidosis
options.C: Urinary retention
options.D: Transitional hyperplasia

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! When a patient feels the urge but can't pass urine and is restless, think urinary retention first. You'll be checking for a distended bladder often in surgical wards!

question: Which symptom is a major danger sign that requires immediate medical help after an abortion?

options.A: Feeling slightly tired in the afternoon
options.B: Light spotting that stops after three days
options.C: Mild cramping for twenty minutes in the morning
options.D: Soaking through two heavy pads per hour for two hours

explanation: Heavy bleeding soaking multiple pads in a short time is a red flag for hemorrhage. Always act fast and notify the doctor on duty! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h4)

question: Which special structure helps single-unit smooth muscle cells contract together as one coordinated sheet?

options.A: Neuromuscular spindles
options.B: Desmosomes
options.C: Dense bodies
options.D: Gap junctions

explanation: Gap junctions act like open doorways between neighboring cells, letting electrical messages zip right through so they all squeeze together in harmony.

question: When programming an electronic IV infusion pump on the ward, what unit of measurement do you normally use?

options.A: Milliliters per hour (mL/hr)
options.B: Liters per 24 hours (L/day)
options.C: Drops per minute (gtt/min)
options.D: Drops per second (gtt/sec)

explanation: Spot on! Pumps are designed to deliver a precise volume of fluid every hour, so we program them in mL/hr.

question: How can a nurse best reassure a patient who has mild pregnancy nausea?

options.A: You must take prescription drugs immediately to protect the fetus.
options.B: Mild nausea and vomiting typically do not harm the developing baby.
options.C: Eating large meals will cure the queasiness within hours.
options.D: The symptoms will disappear completely by the second week.

explanation: Mums worry the baby isn't eating enough. Letting them know that mild early nausea won't hurt their little one brings great peace of mind!

question: What is the difference between a key driver and a change idea?

options.A: Drivers deal only with financial costs, while change ideas deal with clinical medications
options.B: Drivers are primary systems influencing the outcome, while change ideas are specific practical actions to test
options.C: Drivers are chosen by hospital directors, while change ideas are chosen by patients
options.D: Drivers are written on paper, while change ideas are only spoken aloud

explanation: Think of drivers as the big areas we need to influence, while change ideas are the fun, practical steps we actually try out on the ward!

question: As a nurse, what is a key action to take while an intrapleural medication is dwelling in the chest?

options.A: Keeping the chest tube permanently clamped until discharge
options.B: Repositioning the patient regularly to distribute the drug
options.C: Removing the chest dressing to inspect the insertion site
options.D: Flushing the chest drainage system with sterile water hourly

explanation: Brilliant! Turning your patient helps the medication wash over all parts of the pleural space so the treatment works evenly.

question: Which medication is commonly given to kill active parasites hiding in body tissues?

options.A: Metronidazole
options.B: Furosemide
options.C: Penicillin G
options.D: Salbutamol

explanation: Spot on! Metronidazole is the go-to drug for wiping out active, tissue-invading amoebas.

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for someone living with long-term Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: Completely restoring lost declarative memories from childhood
options.B: Training the brain to regrow lost neurons through intense puzzles
options.C: Teaching the patient how to fabricate stories more convincingly
options.D: Maximizing remaining functional independence using environmental aids

explanation: Since memory loss sticks around, we focus on helping them stay safe and independent using daily routines, calendars, and friendly cues.

question: Why might someone know a health practice is dangerous yet continue doing it?

options.A: They enjoy being sick and visiting the primary health clinic
options.B: Nurses failed to write down the instructions on a chalkboard
options.C: Government laws forbid them from changing their personal habits
options.D: Economic, social, or cultural barriers make the healthy choice difficult

explanation: So true! Knowing what to do is only half the battle. Money, culture, and daily struggles often make healthy choices tough to practice.

question: What is the key difference between process evaluation and outcome evaluation?

options.A: Process happens before planning, while outcome happens during assessment
options.B: Process is done by doctors, while outcome is done strictly by patients
options.C: Process looks at activities done, while outcome looks at the final results achieved
options.D: Process measures money spent, while outcome measures the weather

explanation: You got it! Process check-ins ask 'Did we do the activities we planned?' while outcome checks ask 'Did health actually improve?'

question: What does opt-out HIV testing mean during antenatal care?

options.A: The test is performed routinely unless the woman explicitly refuses it.
options.B: Only women with visible clinical symptoms are required to take the test.
options.C: The husband must give written consent before the wife can be tested.
options.D: Testing is completely optional and only done if the patient asks for it.

explanation: Opt-out screening means HIV testing is automatically included in routine prenatal lab work, and patients must actively decline if they do not want it. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h4)

question: What does we mean when we say there is a disease outbreak?

options.A: The total eradication of a chronic illness from a population
options.B: A sudden rise in disease cases above normal expectations
options.C: Any single confirmed case of a rare tropical infection
options.D: A predictable seasonal spike in common malaria cases

explanation: An outbreak simply means more people are getting sick than we usually see for that time and place. You've got this!

question: What must a researcher always get from a patient before collecting any study data?

options.A: Permission from local media
options.B: A monetary donation
options.C: Informed consent
options.D: Medical insurance cards

explanation: Correct! Patients must always voluntarily agree to take part after fully understanding what the study is about.

question: A patient has severe vaginal dryness and painful intercourse after menopause. What is a great first nursing suggestion?

options.A: Refer the patient for emergency psychiatric admission
options.B: Suggest intense cardiovascular exercise to increase estrogen
options.C: Advise immediate discontinuation of all sexual activity
options.D: Recommend regular use of water-based lubricants and moisturizers

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Simple solutions like water-based lubricants and moisturizers offer safe, non-hormonal comfort right away.

question: Why is applied research so helpful in everyday clinical nursing?

options.A: It relies entirely on mathematical formulas instead of patients
options.B: It aims to solve immediate, practical patient care problems
options.C: It never requires ethical approval from an institutional board
options.D: It costs nothing to conduct in a busy hospital ward

explanation: You nailed it! Applied research tackles the real, everyday challenges we face right there at the bedside.

question: What is the clearest sign that a community health project has achieved sustainability?

options.A: International donors continue sending large sums of money
options.B: The primary health clinic closes down due to lack of patients
options.C: The local government takes over the salaries of all foreign staff
options.D: The community continues health practices after project staff leave

explanation: You got it! Sustainability means the good habits and programs keep running successfully even after external helpers have packed up and gone home.

question: Why do we love early detection of health issues during antenatal visits?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of hospital delivery to zero
options.B: It ensures the baby will be born exactly on the due date
options.C: It stops minor issues from developing into severe emergencies
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any medications later

explanation: Spotting small changes early lets us step in quickly before things get dangerous. Great nursing intuition!

question: Why should you give clear practical guidance about death certificates and next steps right after a loss?

options.A: To help overwhelmed relatives navigate the administrative next steps
options.B: To ensure the hospital bed is cleared within ten minutes
options.C: To prevent the family from experiencing any grief at all
options.D: To prove to the family that the nurse is in charge

explanation: Administrative tasks feel impossible when someone is in shock. Clear, gentle guidance takes a huge weight off their shoulders.

question: If a mother is still passing bright red lochia rubra on her fifth day postpartum, what might this mean?

options.A: The expected start of the mother's normal menstrual cycle
options.B: Normal progression of postpartum vaginal discharge
options.C: A potential delay or complication in normal uterine healing
options.D: Complete closure of the internal cervical os

explanation: Normally, bright red discharge only lasts for the first couple of days before turning brownish or pink. Seeing bright red blood on day five is a red flag that healing might be delayed or some tissue was retained. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h2)

question: Which type of law is made through acts passed by government and legislative bodies?

options.A: Common law
options.B: Private law
options.C: Moral law
options.D: Statutory law

explanation: Statutory law simply comes from written laws and acts passed by lawmakers. You'll see this a lot in healthcare regulations!

question: Which action directly stops the spread of waterborne diseases like cholera?

options.A: Administering daily antibiotics to all healthy adults
options.B: Placing infected individuals in strict air isolation
options.C: Conducting passive surveillance at local clinics
options.D: Treating and chlorinating drinking water supplies

explanation: Exactly! If you clean and chlorinate the drinking water, you cut off the main highway that waterborne germs use to enter the human body.

question: Which anti-nausea medication is commonly given as a skin patch behind the ear for motion sickness?

options.A: Metoclopramide
options.B: Aprepitant
options.C: Scopolamine
options.D: Ondansetron

explanation: Spot on! Scopolamine is a popular anticholinergic patch that travels through the skin to prevent motion sickness during travel. Great clinical fact to remember!

question: Which blood marker is commonly measured to help screen for prostate disorders?

options.A: Plasma glucose
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Serum creatinine
options.D: Prostate-specific antigen

explanation: Elevated levels of prostate-specific antigen can indicate inflammation, enlargement, or cancer within the prostate. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h7)

question: What is the main job of a receptor antagonist drug?

options.A: It converts water-soluble hormones into lipid-soluble molecules
options.B: It destroys all hormone-producing glands in the endocrine system
options.C: It binds to the receptor and blocks natural hormones from attaching
options.D: It forces the cell to produce twice as many receptors as normal

explanation: An antagonist is like a person sitting in a reserved cinema seat—they take up the spot so nobody else (no real hormone) can sit there. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h5)

question: Which of the following is a direct consequence of severe undernutrition?

options.A: Rapid increase in bone mineral density
options.B: Muscle wasting and weak immune response
options.C: Lowered risk of developing pressure injuries
options.D: Enhanced ability to fight off surgical infections

explanation: When the body lacks enough nutrients, it breaks down its own muscle tissue for energy and fails to produce enough immune cells to fight infections. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h4)

question: Why do we use air ambulances for patients in remote areas?

options.A: It bridges the gap to advanced medical facilities
options.B: It is always cheaper than ground ambulance transport
options.C: Patients prefer flying over riding in cars
options.D: Hospitals do not accept ground transfers

explanation: Spot on! When patients are far away from big hospitals, air transport moves them quickly so they can get the high-level care they desperately need.

question: Which term describes a fungal infection in the mouth that often presents as white, wipeable patches?

options.A: Dental caries
options.B: Oral candidiasis
options.C: Gingival hyperplasia
options.D: Severe stomatitis

explanation: Oral candidiasis, commonly known as thrush, is an overgrowth of Candida fungus that creates white patches on the oral tissues. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is the normal pH range for human arterial blood?
explanation: Keep this number locked in your memory! A pH of 7.35 to 7.45 keeps body enzymes working smoothly and cells happy.

question: How does the principle of harmony of objectives help a hospital ward?

options.A: It removes the need for performance appraisals entirely
options.B: It forces every nurse to work identical shift schedules
options.C: It ensures all nurses sing together during morning handover
options.D: It helps staff achieve personal goals while meeting hospital aims

explanation: When personal aspirations align with institutional goals, staff are happier and work harder for patient outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h2)

question: A nurse is sent to a remote village with no motorable roads or clinic. What kind of situation is this?

options.A: Single parents with plenty of cash
options.B: Internally displaced persons waiting for homes
options.C: Rural families facing geographic and infrastructure challenges
options.D: Urban rich families taking a break from business

explanation: Spot on! Isolated villages struggle because bad roads and lack of basic infrastructure make it really hard to reach standard healthcare.

question: Which of these is an actual 'system-level' fix to improve patient safety?

options.A: Redesigning electronic medication screens to make high-risk doses harder to select
options.B: Warning all nursing staff to pay closer attention during their shifts
options.C: Posting a memo on the staff bulletin board about being careful
options.D: Suspending the nurse involved in the error for a period of two weeks

explanation: That's a true system fix! Changing how a computer system or tool works makes doing the right thing much easier and mistakes much harder to make.

question: Why is petroleum jelly (Vaseline) gauze usually placed on the wound after a circumcision?

options.A: To dissolve any remaining surgical stitches instantly
options.B: To speed up the natural growth of pubic hair follicles
options.C: To prevent the raw surgical site from sticking to the diaper
options.D: To permanently numb the glans penis against clothing

explanation: Vaseline acts as a gentle, non-stick shield. It keeps the tender healing skin from sticking painfully to the baby's diaper.

question: What is a major risk if a nurse crosses professional boundaries with a home care patient?

options.A: Improving the patient's physical healing speed instantly
options.B: Eliminating all paperwork requirements for the visit
options.C: Guaranteeing a promotion from the nursing agency
options.D: Compromising clinical objectivity and causing burnout

explanation: Well done! When boundaries get blurry, it's easy to lose your professional focus, which leads to emotional fatigue and can affect the quality of your care.

question: Which position usually helps make chest pain feel better when a patient has pericarditis?

options.A: Reclining deeply with legs elevated
options.B: Lying completely flat on the back
options.C: Sitting upright and leaning forward
options.D: Turning sharply onto the left side

explanation: Leaning forward pulls the heart away from surrounding tissues, reducing painful friction and giving the patient sweet relief. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h2)

question: A patient's blood pressure reads 142/92 mmHg in the clinic. Which category does this fall into?

options.A: Stage 1 Hypertension
options.B: Stage 2 Hypertension
options.C: Normal blood pressure
options.D: Elevated blood pressure

explanation: Since both the top number (142) is 140+ and the bottom number (92) is 90+, this climbs into Stage 2 hypertension.

question: How can time pressure in a busy clinic contribute to over-prescription?

options.A: Doctors have more time to carefully review every single medical chart
options.B: Clinicians may quickly write prescriptions to end consultations faster
options.C: Nurses take over all prescribing duties to reduce doctor workload
options.D: Patients automatically leave the clinic without asking for drugs

explanation: When clinics are overcrowded, writing a prescription takes less time than explaining why a drug is not needed. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the main difference between proactive and reactive risk strategies?

options.A: Proactive strategies cost more money than any reactive hospital investigation
options.B: Proactive strategies are handled by doctors, while reactive strategies are handled by nurses
options.C: Proactive strategies act before harm happens, while reactive strategies respond after harm occurs
options.D: Proactive strategies focus on equipment, while reactive strategies focus on staff

explanation: The timing is the key difference: stopping an accident beforehand versus cleaning up the pieces after an accident takes place. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h4)

question: How does nurse involvement in community support networks benefit the broader health system?

options.A: It empowers volunteers and lightens the workload on formal clinic staff
options.B: It restricts patient interactions strictly inside the hospital building
options.C: It ensures that nurses make all decisions without community input
options.D: It eliminates the need for any medications in chronic disease care

explanation: By training community members to help run support networks, health centers extend their reach and ease pressure on busy clinics. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h6)

question: Why do nurse researchers like using histograms for patient data?

options.A: To replace the need for ethical board approval in clinical trials
options.B: To quickly visualize the distribution and spread of a data set
options.C: To prove a causal relationship between two separate nursing interventions
options.D: To track the exact medical record number of every patient in a study

explanation: Turning raw numbers into a clear picture helps you spot patterns and averages at a glance. Simple and super helpful in research!

question: According to cell theory, where do all new cells come from?

options.A: Spontaneous generation
options.B: Extracellular fluid
options.C: Nutrients in the blood
options.D: Pre-existing cells

explanation: Cell theory states that life is continuous because all new cells are formed by the division of older, pre-existing cells. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing consideration related to postpartum endocrine changes?

options.A: Monitoring for sudden increases in maternal blood pressure caused by rising placental hormone levels
options.B: Observing for successful milk let-down reflex stimulated by infant suckling and oxytocin
options.C: Reassuring the mother about normal physiological changes during her hospital recovery
options.D: Assessing for signs of postpartum mood changes linked to rapid estrogen and progesterone withdrawal

explanation: Placental hormone levels drop rapidly after delivery, not rise. Therefore, rising placental hormone levels are not a concern postpartum. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h6)

question: A nurse wants to study fatigue among emergency room nurses. After defining the topic and choosing the hospital, what is the next logical step?

options.A: Select a representative sample of emergency room nurses
options.B: Change the shifts of all nurses in the hospital
options.C: Wait five years to see if the nurses retire
options.D: Write the final conclusion for the research journal

explanation: You can't study everyone, so picking a good, representative group of ER nurses is your next vital step.

question: What is the main purpose of using a Punnett square?

options.A: To check if a patient has an active bacterial infection
options.B: To predict the probability of an offspring inheriting a trait
options.C: To count the exact number of chromosomes in a patient
options.D: To measure the physical length of a single DNA strand

explanation: Clinicians and researchers use Punnett squares to calculate the mathematical odds of passing down specific genetic traits. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is constantly struggling with time management a direct path to burnout for nurses?

options.A: It forces hospital management to give nurses mandatory pay raises
options.B: It gives nurses too much free time, leading to boredom on the ward
options.C: It prevents nurses from ever interacting with patients directly
options.D: It creates constant stress, fatigue, and feelings of inadequacy from unfinished work

explanation: So true. Feeling like you're always behind drains your emotional and physical energy. Be kind to yourself—learning time management is a journey!

question: Why is drinking plenty of water especially critical for a nursing mother?

options.A: Lactation permanently increases core body temperature
options.B: Nursing mothers completely stop feeling thirsty
options.C: Milk production requires extra sodium from blood
options.D: Breast milk is composed mostly of water

explanation: Spot on! Since breast milk is mostly water, nursing mums need extra fluids to keep up their milk supply and stay hydrated.

question: How does effective 'directing' help a clinical nursing team?

options.A: It builds trust, resolves conflicts, and prevents misunderstandings
options.B: It replaces hospital rules and regulations
options.C: It determines how many beds are needed in emergency
options.D: It automatically lowers medication costs

explanation: Good leadership and communication through directing keep the team happy, united, and working well together.

question: Why is patient safety in maternity care uniquely complex?

options.A: Pregnancy completely prevents any physical or medical complications
options.B: The nurse must monitor and protect two distinct lives at the same time
options.C: Labor and delivery wards never experience staffing shortages
options.D: Maternity patients never follow clinical instructions or take medications

explanation: In maternity care, you are caring for both the mother and the baby. That doubles your watch duty and your clinical responsibility!

question: Which of the following actions is NOT appropriate when a nurse discovers a severely irregular pulse in a resting patient?

options.A: Notify the attending physician promptly about the irregular rhythm
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to report the finding
options.C: Review the medication record for heart-altering drugs
options.D: Assess the patient for dizziness, chest pain, or shortness of breath

explanation: Waiting to report an acute abnormal finding puts the patient at risk; abnormal signs require prompt assessment and notification. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h6)

question: What does the psychosocial dimension in palliative care primarily focus on?

options.A: Surgical correction of terminal organs
options.B: Emotional, social, and psychological needs
options.C: Nutritional intake and calorie counting
options.D: Strict measurement of vital signs

explanation: Psychosocial care deals with the mental, emotional, and social well-being of the patient rather than purely physical functions. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h1)

question: A patient comes in with sudden, severe eye pain, headache, vomiting, and seeing rainbow halos around lights. What should you suspect?

options.A: Simple presbyopia
options.B: Open-angle glaucoma
options.C: Closed-angle glaucoma
options.D: Allergic conjunctivitis

explanation: When eye drainage suddenly gets completely blocked, pressure spikes fast. This causes intense pain, nausea, and blurry rainbow halos around lights!

question: What is the main benefit of Continuing Professional Development (CPD) for nurses?

options.A: It keeps nursing skills updated for modern and complex client needs
options.B: It serves as a punishment for making minor documentation errors
options.C: It allows nurses to work indefinitely without taking rest breaks
options.D: It replaces the need for initial professional nursing licensure

explanation: CPD keeps your nursing toolkit fresh! It ensures you stay up to date with new medical practices, technologies, and guidelines.

question: What type of stimuli does our sense of smell (olfaction) pick up?

options.A: Mechanical pressure changes
options.B: Airborne chemical molecules
options.C: Light waves and photons
options.D: Physical sound vibrations

explanation: Great job! Smell is a chemical sense. Tiny, invisible particles floating in the air—called odorants—stimulate receptors in our nose so we can perceive different scents.

question: What is the first step when preparing to share serious news using the SPIKES protocol?

options.A: Setting up a private, quiet space with minimal interruptions
options.B: Giving the patient all test results immediately upon entering
options.C: Asking the family to leave the room for privacy
options.D: Reading the patient's vital signs out loud

explanation: The first step of SPIKES focuses on setting, which involves arranging a private, comfortable environment for the discussion. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h4)

question: A patient has heavy bleeding, bad cramps, an open cervix, and reports that some tissue has passed but parts are still inside. What is this called?

options.A: Threatened abortion
options.B: Missed abortion
options.C: Incomplete abortion
options.D: Septic abortion

explanation: When some tissue comes out but part of it stays trapped inside with an open cervix, we call it an incomplete abortion. Great clinical spotting!

question: What good daily habit should nurses encourage patients to practice regarding bowel movements?

options.A: Waiting until the weekend to try passing stool
options.B: Responding promptly to the natural urge to defecate
options.C: Holding bowel movements until bedtime
options.D: Straining forcefully every morning regardless of urge

explanation: You've got this! Ignoring the call of nature lets the colon suck out more water, making the stool much harder to pass later.

question: What substance is put into a vaccine to trigger the body's immune defense?

options.A: An antibiotic
options.B: A red blood cell
options.C: A plasma protein
options.D: An antigen

explanation: Great job! Vaccines carry harmless pieces of germs called antigens. This teaches your immune system what the real germ looks like without making you sick.

question: What main process causes osmotic diarrhoea?

options.A: Rapid muscle contractions moving food too fast to digest
options.B: Unabsorbed particles staying in the gut and drawing water in
options.C: Bacterial toxins directly forcing salt and water secretion
options.D: Bleeding ulcers leaking protein and blood into the bowel

explanation: Osmotic means pulling water! When certain substances aren't absorbed in your gut, they act like a magnet, drawing water right along with them into your stool.

question: Where does a National Health Insurance Scheme usually get most of its money from?

options.A: Direct cash payments at hospital front desks
options.B: Government taxes and payroll deductions
options.C: Voluntary donations from local businesses
options.D: Monthly loans from commercial banks

explanation: That's correct! National schemes rely on public funds like taxes and mandatory employee contributions to make sure care stays available for everyone.

question: What is the primary underlying cause of inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: Vitamin and mineral deficiencies
options.B: Acute physical trauma to the brain
options.C: Genetic mutations in the DNA
options.D: Severe bacterial infections

explanation: These disorders stem directly from inherited flaws or mutations within the genetic code that disrupt normal cellular function. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h1)

question: How can you easily tell the difference between a child with marasmus and one with kwashiorkor?

options.A: Marasmus causes high fever and rashes, while kwashiorkor causes breathing failure
options.B: Children with kwashiorkor have no body fat loss at all compared to normal children
options.C: Kwashiorkor only affects teenagers, while marasmus only affects newborn infants
options.D: Marasmus children have severe muscle wasting and look very thin, while kwashiorkor children show pitting edema and swelling

explanation: Great job! Marasmus is like severe starvation with extreme thinness, while kwashiorkor features notable swelling (edema) from lack of protein.

question: What is the main reason for plotting a child's weight on a growth chart during clinic visits?

options.A: To check if the child needs immediate dental surgery
options.B: To calculate the exact adult height of the child
options.C: To determine how much money the family earns
options.D: To detect faltering growth early before severe malnutrition develops

explanation: Spot on! Growth charts let us catch weight drops or slow growth early so we can step in long before severe malnutrition sets in.

question: Why is multi-sectoral collaboration necessary for executing a national population policy?

options.A: Local governments have no role in community development.
options.B: Only one government ministry is allowed to handle population matters.
options.C: NGOs and traditional rulers are legally banned from healthcare.
options.D: Population issues impact health, education, and economic sectors simultaneously.

explanation: Population touches everything—health, schools, jobs, and social welfare. Because of this, different sectors and leaders must team up to make real progress.

question: Which tool is best for collecting a clean soil sample for microbial isolation?

options.A: A bare human hand pressed directly onto top dirt
options.B: An unsterilized wooden stick from the ground
options.C: A sterile trowel from a few centimeters below the surface
options.D: A household sponge soaked in soapy water

explanation: Well done! Digging slightly under the topsoil with a sterile tool helps you avoid dried-out dirt and outside germs.

question: Why do many lung cancer patients only discover they are sick when the disease is already advanced?

options.A: The lungs lack pain receptors, allowing tumors to grow undetected initially.
options.B: Symptoms only appear after the cancer completely destroys the heart.
options.C: Early lung tumors cause immediate total paralysis of the limbs.
options.D: Blood tests detect the cancer cells only during late stages.

explanation: You got it! Because lung tissue doesn't have pain nerve endings, a small tumor can grow quietly for a long time without causing any physical pain.

question: What type of joints hold the flat bones of the skull tightly together so they don't move?

options.A: Fibrous joints
options.B: Cartilaginous joints
options.C: Synovial joints
options.D: Symphysis joints

explanation: Exactly! The bones of your skull are tightly locked together by tough fibrous tissue (called sutures) to protect your brain safely.

question: What is a common myth that scares young people away from hormonal contraception?

options.A: It automatically increases an individual's height by ten inches
options.B: It turns eye color into a completely different shade overnight
options.C: It causes permanent internal accumulation or organ rotting
options.D: It cures all forms of infectious diseases instantly

explanation: Baseless fears about pills piling up inside the body are common myths. Patient education clears this right up!

question: What is the very first stop in the brainstem where all taste nerve fibers meet?

options.A: Thalamus
options.B: Nucleus of the solitary tract
options.C: Hypothalamus
options.D: Gustatory cortex

explanation: Taste signals traveling through cranial nerves VII, IX, and X all make their first brainstem stop at the nucleus of the solitary tract in the medulla.

question: What is one of the main everyday duties of a community health nurse?

options.A: Assessing community needs and delivering health education
options.B: Managing national health insurance policies and budgets
options.C: Designing and constructing public water treatment plants
options.D: Performing major orthopedic surgeries in local clinics

explanation: Community nurses spend a lot of time finding out what local health gaps exist and teaching the public how to stay well.

question: What must an assisted living facility do after inspectors find a safety or rule violation during a visit?

options.A: Submit and implement a formal plan of correction
options.B: Immediately close the building and relocate all residents
options.C: Change the state laws to match current facility practices
options.D: Ignore the finding if staff members disagree with it

explanation: Spot on! When inspectors find a problem, the facility has to write down a clear plan showing how they will fix it and make sure it never happens again.

question: What is considered the gold standard procedure for directly viewing pelvic structures and measuring tubal length?

options.A: Abdominal X-ray
options.B: Routine urinalysis
options.C: Transabdominal ultrasound
options.D: Diagnostic laparoscopy

explanation: Laparoscopy lets the surgeon look directly inside the pelvis with a tiny camera, making it the best way to check out the fallopian tubes up close.

question: Why would a doctor give a pregnant patient a tocolytic medication?

options.A: To provide effective pain relief during active labour
options.B: To induce rhythmic contractions for a post-dates labour
options.C: To temporarily halt premature uterine contractions
options.D: To prevent heavy bleeding immediately after delivery

explanation: Think of tocolytics as 'time-buys'—they relax the uterus to slow down early labor and give the baby more time to grow.

question: What is the primary mechanism behind a fat embolism following a long bone fracture?

options.A: Immobility causes fat cells under the skin to melt into the bloodstream
options.B: Infection at the fracture site turns local soft tissues into fatty deposits
options.C: The body stores extra dietary fat in broken bones during the healing phase
options.D: Fat droplets from the bone marrow enter open blood vessels and travel to the lungs

explanation: When a large long bone breaks, yellow bone marrow fat can escape into damaged blood vessels, creating emboli that block small vessels in the lungs and brain. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h6)

question: Where should you tell a patient to place a sublingual tablet?

options.A: Under the tongue
options.B: On top of the tongue
options.C: Swallowed with a full glass of water
options.D: Between the cheek and gum

explanation: You've got it! 'Sub' means under, and 'lingual' means tongue. Slipping it right there lets it melt away and soak straight into the blood vessels.

question: What is the main goal of adding psychosocial support to post-abortion care?

options.A: To diagnose underlying psychiatric disorders through formal testing
options.B: To help patients process emotional distress, fear, and stigma
options.C: To convince patients to testify against unsafe abortion providers
options.D: To provide legal representation for women facing criminal charges

explanation: Spot on! Psychosocial support offers a safe, compassionate space to address the emotional trauma or guilt associated with pregnancy loss.

question: A female patient keeps missing her medication pickups and acts very anxious whenever her husband is mentioned. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Complete indifference to her personal physical wellbeing
options.B: Potential gender-based control or financial dependency affecting care
options.C: An allergic reaction to the prescribed drug packaging
options.D: A simple case of mild seasonal forgetfulness

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! Anxiety and missed visits can be red flags for controlling relationships or a lack of financial freedom at home.

question: Which disease outbreak is most feared in overcrowded camps with poor sanitation?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Appendicitis
options.D: Cholera

explanation: Spot on! Where clean water is scarce and waste management is tough, water-borne bacteria like cholera can cause rapid and dangerous outbreaks.

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge currently facing the nursing profession worldwide?

options.A: Managing chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: Complete elimination of all patient illnesses
options.C: Shortages of qualified nursing personnel
options.D: High rates of workplace stress and burnout

explanation: We haven't wiped out all illnesses yet! Instead, nurses worldwide battle daily with staff shortages, burnout, and rising chronic illnesses.

question: What makes a disease communicable?

options.A: It only affects people living in tropical climates.
options.B: It can be spread from one person or host to another.
options.C: It is caused strictly by genetic mutations in the body.
options.D: It cannot be prevented by standard hygiene practices.

explanation: You've got this! Communicable diseases simply mean infections that can jump or spread from an infected person to someone else. Keep up the great work!
